source.title: Chain of Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Jason Wei; Xue-Zhi Wang; Dale Schuurmans; Maarten Bosma; Ed H. Chi; F. Xia; Quoc V. Le; Denny Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates downstream task accuracy across model sizes, a different measure from the claim’s held-out pretraining loss and fitted scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many downstream reasoning-task accuracies across model sizes. These bear on V6. It does not report pretraining-loss measurements or fit scaling laws. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study reports downstream accuracy across model-size series (PaLM 8B/62B/540B, LaMDA 0.4–137B, GPT-3 0.35–175B). It states explicitly that chain-of-thought success cannot be predicted by extrapolating small models. That bears directly on V6. It measures no pretraining loss and fits no laws, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that chain-of-thought prompting improves arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning, and that this is an emergent ability of scale: it hurts or does nothing below about 10–100B parameters. They add that it lets large models solve tasks where standard prompting has flat scaling curves, and that its success is not predictable by extrapolating small models.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates prompted downstream task accuracy across model sizes; it does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit power laws, or allocate fixed compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompting method and task affect outcomes; the paper also reports variation with exemplar annotator, exemplar selection and order, and number of exemplars.
record.problems: The reported measurements are downstream accuracies, not pretraining losses or fitted scale relationships. The selected PaLM results do not include uncertainty estimates; the paper reports standard deviations for some other prompting experiments. The paper notes that model scale can be conflated with training compute and that results vary by task and prompting setup.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted other model families and checkpoints (LaMDA, GPT, Codex, UL2), PaLM and other model results for additional arithmetic and commonsense breakdowns, symbolic-reasoning evaluations, ablations, and robustness variants. These appear mainly in Appendix Tables 1–7 and Figures 5–8 and 11. The retained rows cover PaLM size series for the five arithmetic and five commonsense benchmarks in Appendix Tables 2 and 4.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No loss extrapolation from small runs.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameters.
No other modalities or training regimes.
The link between downstream performance and pretraining loss, and any fitted predictive curve, is untested. Only accuracy versus parameter count at 3–5 points per family is reported.
No fitted exponents or allocation choices.

missing.what: LaMDA and GPT-3 size series in which CoT hurts small models and standard prompting stays flat on GSM8K and AQuA (e.g. LaMDA GSM8K standard 2.6→6.5; GPT AQuA CoT 8.7, 4.3, 13.4, 35.8).
MAWPS MultiArith subset: PaLM standard 4.2/7.3/42.2 versus CoT 15.8/73.7/94.7, an abrupt non-smooth jump.
Symbolic tasks: OOD length generalisation appears only at 62B+ (last-letter OOD:3 is 0.0→59.6→94.8).
Explicit statement that CoT success cannot be predicted by extrapolating small-scale performance, and that CoT hurts models under 10B.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope reason misstates AQuA: PaLM 62B CoT (22.4) is not below 8B CoT (21.7); it is below 62B standard (25.6). Rows r01–r60 are single points, so per-row cannot_determine is acceptable; the verdicts rest on comparing points within each series. Verdicts use parameter count only; the authors note scale is conflated with training compute. GPT-3 models are InstructGPT variants whose sizes are presumed.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Predicting large-run pretraining loss from fits to smaller runs.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates task accuracy across model sizes, but does not measure pretraining loss, fit a prediction curve, or test whether pretraining loss predicts downstream results.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

relationships.condition: PaLM, standard prompting, most arithmetic and commonsense tasks
relationships.reason: Standard-prompting accuracy rises steadily 8B→62B→540B on GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, CSQA, Date, Sports and SayCan, e.g. GSM8K 4.9→9.6→17.9 (r01,r03,r05).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased steadily on GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, CSQA, Date, Sports and SayCan, including GSM8K from 4.9 to 9.6 to 17.9.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: PaLM, standard prompting, most arithmetic and commonsense tasks
source_check.reason: Tables 2 and 4 show increasing standard-prompting accuracy across PaLM 8B, 62B and 540B for all named tasks. This supports the improvement-with-scale component; quantitative predictive accuracy is not tested.

relationships.reason: CoT accuracy is at or below standard at 8B (GSM8K 4.1 vs 4.9; StrategyQA 53.5 vs 55.6), then jumps sharply at larger sizes. The authors state this success cannot be predicted by extrapolating small models (App. A.1, text-based). Rows: r02,r04,r06,r37,r38.
relationships.display_finding: At 8B, chain-of-thought accuracy trailed standard prompting on GSM8K, 4.1 versus 4.9, and StrategyQA, 53.5 versus 55.6, before larger-model gains that the authors considered unpredictable from smaller models.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.reason: Appendix A.1 explicitly states that small-model extrapolation cannot predict CoT success. Table 2 gives PaLM GSM8K CoT accuracy of 4.1%, 29.9% and 56.9% across 8B, 62B and 540B.

relationships.condition: PaLM, AQuA and StrategyQA, standard prompting
relationships.reason: The scaling curve is flat or non-monotone. AQuA standard is 19.3→25.6→25.2 (r19,r21,r23); StrategyQA standard is only 55.6→58.4→68.6 (r37,r39,r41). AQuA CoT at 62B (22.4) falls below standard (25.6) (r21,r22).
relationships.display_finding: Standard-prompting accuracy changes from 19.3 to 25.6 to 25.2 on AQuA and 55.6 to 58.4 to 68.6 on StrategyQA; at 62B, AQuA chain-of-thought accuracy is 22.4 versus 25.6 with standard prompting.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: PaLM, AQuA and StrategyQA, standard prompting
source_check.reason: Narrow limits_scope to AQuA: standard accuracy is 19.3%, 25.6%, 25.2%. StrategyQA rises monotonically at 55.6%, 58.4%, 68.6% and belongs in a separate supports group. AQuA's 62B CoT-versus-standard comparison does not establish a standard-prompting scaling limitation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study measures downstream reasoning accuracy across model sizes under standard and chain-of-thought prompting, directly bearing on V6.

tranche.reason: Appendix A.1 explicitly argues that small-model performance extrapolation cannot predict successful chain-of-thought reasoning; the size series and prompt-dependent curves qualify V6.

source_check.notes: Individual accuracy points cannot establish a scaling trend, so cannot_determine is appropriate for the listed rows. The study measures no pretraining loss, fits no power laws, and does not test compute-optimal allocation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PaLM across the five arithmetic and five commonsense benchmarks reported in Appendix Tables 2 and 4
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported size series, task accuracies generally rise from 8B to 540B; the rows document the individual measurements (r01–r60). This supports scale-related downstream improvement in these tested settings, not a fitted prediction law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Chain-of-thought prompting on StrategyQA and AQuA, with comparisons across prompt types and sizes
reader_labels.reason: Some task and prompt comparisons are not uniformly increasing at each step: for example, PaLM 8B chain-of-thought accuracy is below standard on StrategyQA, and PaLM 62B chain-of-thought accuracy on AQuA is below its 8B value. The paper also states that chain-of-thought gains emerge only at sufficient scale and cannot be predicted simply by extrapolating small-scale performance.
